hero.title: The Dilemma of Freshness & Sustainability in Puger
hero.description: Explore the Puger ecosystem through the lens of science.

signin.description: Input your Researcher ID to access the Puger Project database.
signin.label: Researcher Identifier (ID)

initial.instruction: Watch the 360° video of the harbor and the interviews with the three stakeholders (Sailor, Seafood Seller, and Government Official).

tips.suffix: for a full 360° experience. Click and drag the video screen to look around the TPI and observe the different stakeholder perspectives.

sailor.label: Sailor
sailor.summary: Complains about the piles of trash getting caught in the nets and boat engines.

seller.label: Seafood Seller
seller.summary: Worries about the quality of fish being contaminated by plastic debris in the harbor.

official.label: Government Official
official.summary: Explains the challenges of regulating waste management in coastal areas.

component_id.title: 1. Component Identification
component_id.description: List at least five physical or biological components you observed in the system (e.g., specific organisms, types of debris, or environmental factors).
component_id.placeholder: Example: Tuna Fish, Plastic Bags, Nylon Nets...

properties.title: 2. Properties
properties.description: Choose two components and describe their properties (e.g., Is it buoyant? Is it persistent? Does it interact with living tissue?).

initial.footer: Make sure all component and property observations are filled in before proceeding to the analysis phase.

qualitative.instruction: Compare a large plastic bottle (seen in the harbor) with a microplastic fiber (mentioned by the Seller).

analysis.q1_desc: What changes in shape and size do you observe as the plastic breaks down from a bottle to microplastic fibers?
analysis.q2_desc: What environmental factors (e.g., UV exposure, wave abrasion) might contribute to the breakdown of macroplastics into microplastics?
analysis.q3_desc: How do the characteristics of microplastics differ from those of macroplastics in terms of their interactions with marine life and their persistence in the environment?

qualitative.footer: This qualitative analysis will be the basis for quantitative calculations in the next phase.

quantitative.instruction: Pay attention to the data table on the abundance of microplastics in various areas in Jember from rivers to beaches.

questions.q1_desc: Why does concentration drop at Station 4 but spike at Station 3? Link this to river runoff vs ocean currents.
questions.q2_desc: Based on Station 2, estimate particles ingested if a human drinks 2L of water/day.
questions.q3_desc: Calculate BMF between Cockles and Tuna. If a person eats 250g of cockles/week, how many mg of plastic is ingested?

placeholders.q1: Explain the interaction between runoff and currents...

explanation.ar_setup_desc: Use the 'Cellular Impact' module for desktop how plastic polymers interact with cell membranes and organ systems.
explanation.qualitative_desc: Explain how plastic bottles (macro) from ports become cellular hazards. Consider the roles of UV radiation, wave abrasion, and cell membrane penetration.
explanation.quantitative_desc: If fishermen use contaminated ice by the kilo every day, calculate the potential annual plastic burden on local residents who consume fish regularly.

placeholders.qualitative: Analysis of atmospheric, aquatic, and cellular interactions...
placeholders.quantitative: Use plastic load data (mg/kg) to calculate annual accumulation...

decision.instruction: You are a consultant to a government official. You must propose a strategy to reduce microplastic levels (e.g., a “Microfilter Act” for washing machines or a “Plastic Tax”).

labels.social_impact_desc: Social Impact of the Seafaring Community

questions.conclusion_desc: Why is this systemic solution more effective than just a professional-scale 'Beach Cleanup'?

placeholders.general: Impact analysis from a consultant's perspective...
placeholders.final: Synthesis of why upstream prevention is better than downstream cleanup...
